prompt: Number each user's sessions on 26 October 2025, the day the clocks went back (the UTC day of event_ts). Use only that day's app events, so each user's first event of the day starts session 1. A user's first app event starts a session, and an event more than 30 minutes after the same user's previous event starts a new one; an event exactly 30 minutes later stays in the same session. Measure each gap as the time between the two moments in event_ts, a UTC instant, never between clock times. Return four columns, in this order: event_id, user_id, event_ts and session_no, the number of the session the event belongs to, counting from 1 for each user. Return one row for each event. Any row order is fine.

output_contract.grain: one row per app event on 26 October 2025 (UTC)

hints: Next, flag each event that starts a session, then add the flags up in each user's time order.
The session number is a running SUM of the 1s and 0s, per user, from the first row up to the current one.
faded_shape:

  SELECT event_id, user_id, event_ts,
